text:
mia: starting staged canary rl-2026-03-20-01 now at 5% — launching in the 18:00 PST change window. eu region intentionally blocked for initial smoke. tagging @raj @olivia for watch

deploy-bot: rollout rl-2026-03-20-01 started by mia — id=rl-2026-03-20-01, from=v1.2.2, to=v1.2.3, traffic=5%, regions=[us-west1,us-east1], eu=blocked

raj: saw a small latency blip on us-west at 18:03 — p95 120ms -> 210ms for a 3m span. errors stable though (0.04%). checking traces and tail logs now.

olivia: noticing mem pressure on gpu-pool-2 around the same timeframe, a couple of OOM events recovered by kube. not sure if related to batch size.

sre-oncall: recommend HOLD at 5% until we confirm mem spike is transient. prefer pinning eu and stopping any further ramp until we clear this.

mia: agree — HOLD and PIN. can we pin eu traffic back to v1.2.2 and prevent further percent increases? want to avoid cross-region rollouts while investigating. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: action: pin-region rl-2026-03-20-01 eu -> pinned_to=v1.2.2 (success). global rollout remains at 5% and ramp disabled.

anne: quick mitigation suggestion: reduce inference batch_size from 16 -> 12 for v1.2.3 and re-evaluate. that should lower mem tail while preserving throughput. can test the change in staging first.

raj: kicking off staging perf job with batch_size=12 now. running 1000 requests, measuring p95 and mem usage. ETA ~10m.

mia: holding calling card — wait for staging perf results and prod 15m signal. if p95 stays >180ms in prod for next 15m, rollback full canary.

deploy-bot: staging perf finished for v1.2.3 (batch_size=12): p95=165ms, mem stable, no OOMs. tagging build v1.2.3-batch12 for a limited re-eval.

sre-oncall: I still prefer a rollback if we see repeat >200ms on prod within next 15m. contingency plan ready: /deploy rollback rl-2026-03-20-01 --to v1.2.2 (manual) or autorollback if alerts cross threshold.

olivia: watching dashboards (gpu-pool-2, request p95, error-rate). will post updates. :eyes:

mia: thanks all — back in ~12m with go/no-go. appreciate the quick response.
